document.title: Usama bin Ladin: Islamic Extremist Financier
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Terrorism and U.S. Policy
document.note: [Unclassified] CIA assessment released to the media in 1996. It gives background on bin Ladin, including his role in supporting the resistance to the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan. It covers his terrorist activities, the Islamic Salvation Foundation (Al-Qaida) and collaboration with other extremist groups. It also traces his commercial activities since 1989 (e.g., construction of an airport near Port Sudan) and reports that by January 1994 he was helping finance three terrorist training camps in northern Sudan.

mentions.quote: Usama bin Muhammad bin Awad Bin Ladin is one of the most significant financial sponsors of Islamic extremist activities in the world today.

organizations.name: al-Qaida
organizations.notes: Founded by 1985 by Bin Ladin to recruit, transport, and train Arab volunteers; ran recruitment centers and guesthouses in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and training camps in Afghanistan/Pakistan.

organizations.name: Bin Ladin Group
organizations.notes: Family construction empire founded by Muhammed Bin Ladin.

organizations.name: National Islamic Front
organizations.notes: Led by Hasan al-Turabi; hosted Bin Ladin and partnered in business.

organizations.name: al-Gama'at al-Islamiyyah
organizations.notes: Egyptian extremist group; worked with al-Qaida on training camps.

organizations.name: al-Jihad
organizations.notes: Claimed to receive Bin Ladin funding.

organizations.name: Al-Hijrah for Construction and Development, Ltd.
organizations.notes: Bin Ladin company; built Tahaddi road and Port Sudan airport; works with Sudanese military to supply training camps.

organizations.name: Taba Investment Company, Ltd.
organizations.notes: Gained near monopoly over Sudanese agricultural exports.

organizations.name: Al-Themar al-Mubarakah Agriculture Company, Ltd.
organizations.notes: Large land holdings near Khartoum and eastern Sudan.

organizations.name: Al-Shamal Islamic Bank
organizations.notes: Capitalized by Bin Ladin ($40 million) and NIF members.

organizations.name: Advisory and Reformation Committee
organizations.notes: London-based dissident organization; issued over 350 pamphlets by July 1995.

organizations.name: INTERPOL
organizations.notes: Yemen reportedly sought its help to apprehend Bin Ladin in 1994.

events.description: Soviet invasion of Afghanistan; Bin Ladin joined Afghan resistance shortly after.
By 1985 Bin Ladin had founded al-Qaida to recruit and train Arab volunteers.
Soviets withdrew; Bin Ladin returned to Jeddah business; Saudis held his passport 1989-1991.
Bin Ladin relocated to Sudan, welcomed by Hasan al-Turabi.
Attempted bombings against some 100 US servicemen in Aden; perpetrators claimed Bin Ladin financed them.
Bin Ladin financed travel of 300-480 Afghan war veterans to Sudan after Pakistani crackdown.
Joint Egyptian-Saudi investigation found Bin Ladin business interests funneled money to Egyptian extremists.
Riyadh revoked Bin Ladin's Saudi citizenship; he formed the Advisory and Reformation Committee.
Eldest brother Bakr Bin Ladin publicly condemned Usama's extremist activities on behalf of the family.
Ramzi Yousef apprehended.
Soviet invasion of Afghanistan; Bin Ladin joined the Afghan resistance shortly after.

Attempted bombings against some 100 U.S. servicemen in Aden; perpetrators claimed Bin Ladin financed them.
World Trade Center bombing, alleged mastermind Ramzi Ahmed Yousef.
Bin Ladin financed travel of 300-480 Afghan war veterans from Pakistan to Sudan.
Joint Egyptian-Saudi investigation revealed Bin Ladin business interests funneled money to Egyptian extremists.
Bin Ladin had begun financing at least three terrorist training camps in northern Sudan.
Riyadh revoked Bin Ladin's Saudi citizenship; he then formed the Advisory and Reformation Committee in London.
Bakr Bin Ladin publicly denounced Usama on behalf of the family.
Ramzi Ahmed Yousef apprehended.
Al-Jihad leader interview claiming Bin Ladin funded the group.

key_claims: Bin Ladin was a leading financier of Islamic extremist activity, founding al-Qaida by 1985 to recruit, transport and train Arab volunteers.
Bin Ladin relocated to Sudan in 1991 under NIF leader al-Turabi's welcome, with business ties to NIF members.
Bin Ladin financed training camps in northern Sudan with Sudanese military and NIF cooperation.
Bin Ladin funded Egyptian groups al-Jihad and al-Gama'at al-Islamiyyah, including a camp in Kunar.
Bin Ladin-funded Peshawar guesthouse housed Ramzi Yousef.
Saudi Arabia revoked his citizenship in 1994 and his family publicly denounced him.
